name: Cosy Night Pixel Art
description: Soft low-light pixel art: crisp visible square pixels in a gentle limited palette of night blues, lavender and warm light, low contrast, and calm uncluttered compositions.
style_bible: Pixel art built at a low logical resolution and scaled up, so that every pixel is a visible square. Medium and surface: hand-placed pixels on a regular grid; diagonals show clean aliased stair-stepping, every edge is hard, and there is no anti-aliasing, no smoothing and no soft gradient anywhere — values change in discrete steps and, where two steps need bridging, a small amount of ordered dithering does it. Palette: one small fixed ramp — three or four night blues from the mid-blue down to blue-violet, two lavenders, and two or three warm light tones — used consistently so the whole picture reads as one coherent set of colours. Value: deliberately low contrast. The lightest tone stays a soft cream rather than pure white and the darkest a deep blue-violet rather than black, so nothing on the screen glares. Lighting: one or two small warm pools of light, with the rest of the frame staying cool and quiet; light falls in stepped pixel bands rather than as a gradient. Composition: calm, simple and uncluttered, with generous areas of flat pixel colour and detail concentrated where the light is. This is a soft, restful register rather than a playful one. No game interface of any kind: no HUD, no health bar, no inventory grid, no dialogue box, no tileset, no side-scrolling platform arrangement, no character sprite in action. No lettering, numbers or captions.
